column1: # Does the stock game enter a conversation at all? Seeded at Britain (4,10)
# with a dialog-id 12 NPC directly west at (3,10). Paired with
# `town-talk-nonspeaker`, which puts a dialog-id 0 NPC under the same
# Seeded rather than walked to. The walk-up form of this scenario scripted its
# way in from the town gate, and the resident walks its own schedule while
# those steps run, so the two sides arrived with it in different cells and
# every later beat compared unrelated windows (`cleak/u5-engine#22`).
# `qa/tools/reseed.py` replayed that walk once into the seed named below.
# **No coin at this seed (measured 2026-10-16).** Earlier revisions
# of this header excused the opening as `conversation.md` Section 9 step 3's
# stranger-introduction coin. This NPC never reaches that coin: its Description
# entry transfers into a label head that asks the party's name (`0x88`), and on
# the dismissive answer prints `Good day!"` and ends on `0x82`, which Section 9
# step 2 makes a stop - "the opener returns and nothing further is printed".
# Sixteen stock runs from 2026-09-12 to 2026-10-16 show the same `name` beat
# every time: the question, `:NAME`, `"If you say so...`, `Good day!"` and the
# command prompt, after which the typed `JOB` is read as `J` (`Jimmy-`). The
# engine followed the description's transfer only from the rc1 merges onward,
# and ran on into `Your interest?` until the fix on branch `triage-town-talk`.
# rc4 sweep (20261020-154909), beat `talk`: after the spec2 conversation
# merges the engine printed the label handler's HEAD quote (`conversation.md`
# §7.7) as a lone `"` row and padded a blank under it before the ASK-WHO
# question's own quote. The stock prints one quote: the head opens on ASK-WHO,
# whose own opening quote the byte runner drops after the HEAD quote (§7.6),
# so `"What is thy name?"` follows the description's blank row directly.
